title: How Trading Barriers in Underlying Asset Markets Impact ETF Trading and Characteristics

authors.name: Jinhwan Kim
authors.affiliation: College of Business Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Hoon Cho
authors.affiliation: College of Business Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Sangik Seok
authors.affiliation: College of Business Administration University of Ulsan

abstract: We examine the impact of the underlying market’s minimum trading unit (MTU) on the corresponding exchange-traded fund (ETF) market using unique hand-collected data. MTUs act as trading barriers, affecting market accessibility. Our findings show that institutional investors are less active in ETFs when the underlying market is less accessible. Improved accessibility in the underlying market correlates with increased arbitrage activity, better tracking ability, and a higher probability of informed trading in ETFs. After a reduction in the underlying market’s MTU, institutional trading in ETFs gradually increases, accompanied by significant changes in arbitrage activity, tracking ability, and informed trading probability.
